park: Solport Convention Center · park under the sun

Thirty-five steel canopies carry the panels that run the campus and shade every bay. Golf carts park two to a bay and charge from the seventy pedestals while their owners are at the summit; the few car bays are by the connector to the Flight Line Gate road and by the Shuttle Hub, where the accessible bays are. The walk along the Market Hall takes you to its doors and on to the arena and the Festival Grounds.
hub: Grand Loop · bike share · cart share · drop-off

The Grand Loop electric shuttle calls here on every lap, then runs to the Convention Center drop-off, Link Plaza and the Stellar Aviation FBO, round all three stages to Main Street and the Commons and back. The board shows the next shuttle. Bikes and carts are free to borrow: leave them in any share bay.
ev: Solar Cart Park · charge under the canopy

Every pedestal has two cables and serves the green bays beside it, carts and the odd electric car alike. The canopies above feed the chargers by day; the campus battery carries them through the night.
charge: The screen wakes, the ring turns green and the canopy overhead does the rest. A full charge while you are at the summit.
garden: Solport Convention Center · a working desert farm

Raised timber and corten beds of chiles, squash, herbs, greens and tomatoes, rows of corn, a citrus, pomegranate and olive orchard and a hoop greenhouse, all on drip lines. Everything goes fifty metres to the Market Hall kitchens, and what is left goes on the farm stand.
greenhouse: Market Garden · seedlings and winter greens
Twin-wall glazing on galvanised hoops. Every bed in the garden starts here as a seedling tray, and the winter greens grow here through the cold months.
orchard: Navel oranges and Meyer lemons, Wonderful pomegranates and olives for the Market Hall's own oil, each tree on its own ring of mulch and its own drip emitter.
coop: Market Garden · eggs for the Market Hall
Six hens and a raised coop with nest boxes. They eat the kitchen scraps, turn the compost and lay the eggs for the Market Hall's breakfast menu.
compost: Market Garden · nothing leaves the campus
Three bays: fresh, turning and finished. Kitchen scraps from the Market Hall, chicken litter and garden trimmings go in; finished compost goes back on the beds.

farmer.name: Marisol
greet: Everything here is grown 50 m from Desert Kitchen.

talk.t: Welcome to the Market Garden. Everything you see is grown 50 m from Desert Kitchen and the rest of the Market Hall: chiles, squash, corn, greens, tomatoes, herbs, citrus and eggs.
o: How do you farm in the desert?
What goes to the Market Hall?

talk.t: Raised beds full of compost, drip lines under every plant and shade from the trellises. Not a drop is wasted: the water goes to the roots, never into the air. The greenhouse starts every seedling.
Most of it. Rosa at Desert Kitchen takes the chiles, corn and squash for her bowls, the coffee bar gets the citrus, and the eggs go to breakfast. The kitchens send their scraps back for the compost.
The farm stand is right here. Whatever the kitchens did not take this morning is on the counter.
